title: introduce-budgeted-prefetch-governor-and-quantile-compression-profiles
author: Asha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Reduce per-token unit cost for mixed-latency workloads by moving from static prefill heuristics to a budget-aware prefetch controller and to introduce a lightweight quantile-based compression registry for compact model snapshots. This PR implements a controller that schedules prefetch/prefill work based on two orthogonal budgets: per-request latency budget and weekly cost budget. The controller exposes tunables via the Console and can be overridden per-route. We also introduce 'quantile compression' profiles — a complementary approach to existing quantization profiles that focuses on compressing KV/attention state snapshots using empirically-derived quantile mappings to reduce memory and I/O without reworking model kernels.

Design & changes in one paragraph: The BudgetedPrefetchGovernor is a new component in serving/prefetch that monitors real-time latency SLO headroom and a rolling cost allowance; it converts those signals into soft prefetch quotas. It integrates with the existing batch scheduler by tagging requests with a 'prefetch priority' and queuing prefetch jobs onto low-priority worker pools. On the quant side, the QuantileCompressionRegistry holds lightweight, versioned mappings and a small runtime that applies a deterministic encode/decode step for KV snapshots; it is API-compatible with the existing quant profile registry so fallbacks are automatic.

Backwards compatibility: zero-downtime. The governor defaults to a conservative mode that mirrors previous behavior (no added prefetch), and quantile profiles are opt-in via model annotation. Merged to main after a staged rollout (canary -> 10% -> 100%).

Testing & validation: unit tests for quota math and compact encoding, integration E2E where a representative conversational workload was replayed (see test traces attached in CI), and a small canary on Dedicated. Observed improvements in unit cost for bursty conversational traces: median token-cost down ~7% and 95th latency increase below 1% when budgets favor cost. Cost-first mode can reduce median token-cost up to 17% for tail-heavy workloads at the expense of ~5-8% tail latency (configurable).

Rollout plan checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] canary with telemetry hooks, [x] console UX toggle added, [x] docs/rfc drafted. Follow-ups: an analytic job to surface candidate quantile mappings from replay logs (ENG-2249), and an autoscaler hook to expose more graceful worker pool expansion under transient load.

Related: linear ENG-2147 (budgeted prefetch controller), ENG-2193 (quantile compression research). See RFC: docs/rfc/budgeted-prefetch.md and implementation notes in serving/prefetch/README.md.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Please add more granularity to the quota math docs; what happens when both budgets are exhausted?
Asha Kapoor: Response: Governor emits a 'budget-exhausted' telemetry event and drops to conservative prefetching; added clarification in docs and unit tests for that transition.
Raya Singh: The quantile encode/decode looks promising but check threading in codec.go; potential allocation hotspots on high concurrency.
Asha Kapoor: Fixed by moving to a sync.Pool-backed buffer and added a benchmark showing <3% CPU overhead at 4k RPS.
Tomás Mejía: CI flaked on the e2e replay; can you stabilize the fixture?
Asha Kapoor: Stabilized fixture by switching to deterministic RNG seed and retrying the CI job; rerun passed.
release_notes: Add Budgeted Prefetch Governor (opt-in) to regulate prefetching based on latency and cost budgets; add Quantile Compression profiles for compact KV snapshot storage. Console exposes per-route budget controls. Improvements: median token unit-cost reduction in bursty conversational workloads; opt-in quantile compression reduces KV footprint for many models.
